question: Does the natural two-local-lapse extension of the frozen equal-endpoint Starobinsky m=2 midpoint action possess the exact finite-dimensional gauge null direction required to treat its relative lapse as a BFV gauge mode?

planner.missing_typed_object: source-defined regulated joint relative class with a same-model finite-m2 BFV source

human_review.bounded_output: one exact scoped verdict on the naive midpoint two-local-lapse unfixing only
human_review.principal_false_signal: mistaking a numerical Hessian sample for a certified stationary point, or promoting failure of this one configuration-space extension to a no-go for every first-order, perfect, improved, or continuum-first BFV construction
human_review.independent_control: certify a unique exact stationary point by a strict Krawczyk inclusion using Arb ball arithmetic, then certify the full extended Hessian determinant excludes zero
human_review.user_authorization_context: the user directed sequential construction and independent mathematical review of the Starobinsky m=2 FP/BFV source before downstream zero-lapse, cover, end and completeness work

frozen_model.name: equal-endpoint two-segment midpoint Starobinsky minisuperspace configuration regulator

candidate_extension.necessary_gauge_condition: an off-shell differentiable gauge identity with a nonzero generator at an exact stationary point requires a Hessian null vector there
not_present: canonical momenta or a first-order constraint lattice
BFV ghosts, multiplier pair, charge or gauge fermion
source equality or deformation to a physical original cycle

certificate.method: strict Krawczyk inclusion for grad(S2)=0 followed by Arb interval determinant exclusion
required_tests: Krawczyk image is strictly inside the frozen box
det(H_S2) excludes zero throughout the frozen box
K and 8*pi^2*K/T^3 exclude zero throughout the frozen box
det(H_Sloc at r=0) excludes zero throughout the frozen box

decision_table.condition: the local-lapse restriction and Hessian block identities are exact, the Krawczyk operator certifies one unique stationary point, the full extended Hessian is certified invertible there, and the declared relative-lapse generator has nonzero r component
the frozen algebra remains valid but the interval certificate does not establish the nondegeneracy required for the scoped KILL row; failure to certify is not evidence of a gauge null direction
